after.jp: 祭りで着物を着る人が多い

structure_explanation.en: The structure uses a relative clause that modifies a noun. 着物を着る ('who wears a kimono') comes before 人 (person) and functions as an adjectival phrase: 'the person who wears a kimono'. 祭りで indicates the place with で. This group 着物を着る人 is the subject marked by が, and the predicate is the い-adjective 多い (they are many).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura usa uma oração relativa que modifica um substantivo. 着物を着る ('que veste quimono') vem antes de 人 (pessoa) e funciona como uma frase adjetiva: 'a pessoa que veste quimono'. 祭りで indica o local com で. Esse grupo 着物を着る人 é o sujeito marcado por が, e o predicado é o adjetivo-い 多い (são muitas).

ops.issue: 四人 (four people) is read よにん, an irregular reading; よんにん is incorrect. The kana transcription teaches a wrong pronunciation.
In the counter compound 四人 the numeral 四 is read よ (yo-nin), not よん. Token reading propagates the wrong pronunciation.
Romaji inherits the wrong reading of 四人: should be yonin (よにん), not yonnin.

before.jp: 私の家族は四人だ
before.kana: わたしのかぞくわよんにんだ

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has the structure 'topic は + predicate だ': 私の家族は (as for my family) is the topic and 四人だ (are four people) is the predicate. The counter 人 (にん) counts people and attaches to the number 四 (four). だ is the informal 'to be'. The focus of this sentence is the vocabulary 家族 (family).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase tem a estrutura 'tópico は + predicado だ': 私の家族は (quanto à minha família) é o tópico e 四人だ (são quatro pessoas) é o predicado. O contador 人 (にん) conta pessoas e se junta ao número 四 (quatro). だ é o 'ser/estar' informal. O foco desta frase é o vocabulário 家族 (família).

ops.issue: 'As for the night' wrongly mirrors 夜に as a topic (は) construction; に here marks time, and there is no topic particle. lit_pt correctly renders it as 'À noite (に)'; lit_en should match.

before.jp: 夜にお風呂に入る
before.kana: よるにおふろにはいる

structure_explanation.en: Simple present sentence with no explicit subject (implied 'I'). The target is the vocabulary お風呂に入る ('to take a bath', literally 'to enter the bath'). The first に marks the time ('at night') and the second に marks the destination of the movement of 'entering'. In Japanese the verb always comes at the end.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Frase simples no presente sem sujeito explícito (subentendido 'eu'). O alvo é o vocabulário お風呂に入る ('tomar banho', literalmente 'entrar no banho'). A primeira に marca o tempo ('à noite') e a segunda に marca o destino do movimento de 'entrar'. Em japonês o verbo vem sempre no fim.

ops.issue: 'to feel' is not a sense of 考える (to think, to consider); in this sentence 考えられている means 'is thought/believed'. The pt gloss 'pensar, achar' is correct; the en gloss should not include 'feel'.

before.jp: 犬は人の気持ちが分かると考えられている
before.kana: いぬわひとのきもちがわかるとかんがえられている

structure_explanation.en: The topic 犬は ('dogs') opens the sentence; within the quoted content, 人の気持ちが分かる ('to understand people's feelings') uses が to mark what is understood, the typical pattern of 分かる. That clause is quoted by と and handed to 考える. The grammatical target is と考えられている (passive 考える + 〜ている), with the impersonal reading 'it is believed/thought that.'
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O tópico 犬は ('os cachorros') abre a frase; dentro do conteúdo citado, 人の気持ちが分かる ('entender os sentimentos das pessoas') usa が para marcar aquilo que se entende, padrão típico de 分かる. Essa oração é citada por と e entregue a 考える. O alvo gramatical é と考えられている (考える passivo + 〜ている), com leitura impessoal de 'acredita-se / pensa-se que'.

translation_literal.en: As for the dog, 'that it understands people's feelings' is thought (by everyone).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao cachorro, 'que (ele) entende os sentimentos das pessoas' é pensado (por todos).

translation.en: Dogs are believed to understand people's feelings.
translation.pt-BR: Acredita-se que os cachorros entendem os sentimentos das pessoas.
